claim: Fast symptom matching sits at Rasmussen's rule-based level: a sign triggers a stored rule without checking the wider system state; the knowledge-based route is the slow fallback.
agent_test: Compare a first-match answer with a forced model-based check on seeded fault cases at equal tokens.

claim: Models trained or prompted on text adopt surface heuristics (lexical overlap) and fail near-totally when the heuristic points the wrong way (HANS: most models under 10% where chance is 50%; BERT 0% on subject/object swap).
agent_test: Build matched cases where the surface cue contradicts the true fault; measure accuracy with and without a cue-check step.

claim: Irrelevant but plausible-looking context sharply cuts LLM accuracy: GSM-IC no more than 18% of solved problems stay solved across distractor types; GSM-NoOp drops up to 65% (o1-preview -17.5); ADDSENT F1 75 to 36.
agent_test: Insert distractor symptoms into diagnosis prompts; test a relevance-filter step against baseline at equal tokens.

claim: Newer models are not immune to distractors: the GSM-NoOp paper reports recent models decline more than older ones in one figure caption; strong models (o1-preview, o1-mini) still drop significantly.
agent_test: Rerun the distractor set on the current model and compare with older baselines.

claim: Mitigations for distraction help only partly: self-consistency and an ignore-irrelevant instruction raise GSM-IC micro accuracy (COT 72.4 to 77.8 with instruction), yet best macro accuracy stays at 45%; eight shots of the same NoOp question did not fix GSM-NoOp.
agent_test: Test instruction plus sampling vote versus a separate cue-filter pass at equal tokens.

claim: Suggested-answer and user-opinion cues pull LLMs toward wrong answers: Turpin up to -36.3 points (GPT-3.5, suggested answer, zero-shot CoT), Sharma up to -27% when a user suggests a wrong answer; CoT explanations do not mention the cue.
agent_test: Add a hidden wrong hint to cases; check whether a cue-audit step removes the drop.

claim: Chain-of-thought does not reliably remove cue sensitivity: Turpin few-shot CoT still -24.1/-21.5; Claude 1.0 sensitivity to always-A improves with CoT (63.2 to 80.1%) but GPT-3.5 barely (55.2 to 58.7%).
agent_test: Compare with and without CoT under planted cues across two model families.

claim: Option-position and prompt-order cues create large accuracy swings: llama-30B picks A/B/C/D 34.6/27.3/22.3/15.8% on balanced labels; moving the answer to D drops gpt-3.5-turbo 67.2 to 60.9; label-free permutation debiasing (PriDe, prior from about 5% of samples) helps; explicit debias instruction and CoT did not remove it.
agent_test: Shuffle candidate-cause order and vote across permutations; measure agreement and accuracy.

claim: Position of relevant evidence matters: accuracy is U-shaped over document position, and the worst middle position can fall below closed-book (GPT-3.5-turbo 56.1%); premise order changes drop accuracy 20-30% or more.
agent_test: Reorder symptoms and logs in the diagnosis prompt; measure variance across orderings.

claim: In-context shortcuts hurt larger models more in one study: GPT2-large dropped 33.71% on anti-shortcut sets versus 1.04% for GPT2-base (common-word shortcut: 63.46 to 22.01 on MR).
agent_test: Plant a frequent but wrong keyword in few-shot exemplars; check if a shortcut-check step helps.

claim: Output and input probability act as a surface cue: GPT-4 decodes a cipher 51% when the answer is a high-probability sequence versus 13% when low; rare tasks near 0% versus common versions high.
agent_test: Test diagnosis of common versus rare faults with matched structure.

claim: Counterfactual variants of familiar tasks degrade LLMs while humans stay high, pointing to reliance on familiar surface forms (GPT-3.5 program parse 99% to 62-75%; analogy tasks degrade for GPT-3/3.5/4).
agent_test: Use unfamiliar re-skinned fault scenarios with the same logic.

claim: LLMs show human-like content (belief) effects on logic: believable invalid conclusions are accepted more; direction matches humans, per-model sizes not recorded.
agent_test: Test believable-but-invalid diagnostic inferences with and without a validity check.

claim: Medical LLMs lose accuracy under cognitive-bias framing: BiasMedQA mean drop false consensus 24.9, frequency 18.2, recency 12.9, confirmation 8.1 points; GPT-4 most resilient (worst -14.0).
agent_test: Same biased-prompt set against the scaffold at equal tokens.

claim: Bias-education style prompts give only partial and model-dependent gains in LLMs (GPT-4 frequency 0.627 to 0.720; Mixtral and GPT-3.5 marginal).
agent_test: Compare a bias-awareness prompt versus a structural step.

claim: Irrelevant clinical wording and patient voice reduce LLM accuracy: MedDistractQA 1.3-17.9% drops; patient-voice retellings -9.6 points (95% CI -11.0 to -8.2) across 12 open models, no scale benefit.
agent_test: Add a normalize-input stage and measure the gap at equal tokens.

claim: Rewriting the input in a neutral standard form first halves the voice penalty (+3.9 points in 11 models), while a structured-schema extraction pipeline was 7.1 points worse than rewrite-then-reason. CoT plus debiasing instructions removed only about a fifth of the gap. (Update: two-step rephrase or context regeneration also helps on general and distractor tasks, but weak models can lose accuracy.)
agent_test: Rewrite-then-reason versus schema extraction on our diagnosis cases; strongest direct S1 test.

claim: In agentic clinical diagnosis, models under-seek information and stay anchored: best of 32 models 68%; data utilization fell 57% to 26% in round 3; 65.6% of wrong first diagnoses stayed wrong.
agent_test: Measure information requests and recovery after a wrong first guess in our agent.

claim: Human clinical studies: teaching bias awareness and cognitive forcing strategies does not reduce diagnostic error (Sherbino 2014 N=191 students, p=.91/.98; O'Sullivan 2019 N=76, 2.8 vs 3.1, p=.49); Norman 2017 review says bias-recognition teaching is ineffective.
agent_test: Do not rely on a beware-of-bias instruction alone; test structural checks.

claim: Reflection helps in some human settings: structured reanalysis restored accuracy after availability bias in second-year residents (Mamede 2010, N=36), and guided reflection was effective in 5 studies of a 28-study review; but speed versus reflect instructions showed no difference (44.5 vs 45.0, snippet only).
agent_test: Compare a structured differential-reanalysis step with a quick first-match path at equal tokens.

claim: Expertise shifts perception to deep structure (Chi 1981 physics sorting, not re-opened) while Take-The-Best matched regression accuracy (.691 vs .694) using about one fifth of cue values, so fast cue use is not always an error.
agent_test: Check task conditions where cheap cue use suffices versus where cues mislead; gate the deep check on cue validity.

claim: Diagnostic prompt style barely matters for GPT-4 on clinical vignettes (CoT 76, intuitive 77, differential 78, Bayesian 72); GPT-3.5 loses with differential/Bayesian prompts.
agent_test: Compare reasoning styles inside our scaffold.

claim: LLM agents for root-cause analysis struggle with evidence quality: ReAct 35% correct, hallucination 4% vs CoT 12% vs retrieval 40%, 66% of ReAct wrong answers were insufficient information; RCAgent ablation shows observation handling matters (pass rate down 33.54% without KV storage).
agent_test: Ablate observation storage and evidence summarization in our agent.

claim: Sycophancy: models change first answers in 32% (GPT-4) to 86% (Claude 1.3) of are-you-sure cases, a cue-following failure relevant to premature acceptance of user hints.
agent_test: Plant user pushback and test a hold-position check.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Hiding the raw input from the answering step is what makes rewrite-then-reason work: S2A with the original context kept scored 74.5% vs 80.3% (oracle 82.0%, baseline 62.8%) on LLaMA-2-70B-chat; an ignore-irrelevant instruction gave 71.7% on opinion prompts and no consistent gain on GSM-IC.
agent_test: Compare rewrite-only-visible vs rewrite-plus-original vs instruction-only at equal tokens on seeded cue-conflict faults.

claim: Intrinsic self-recheck without new evidence does not fix errors and often hurts: GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1 after one self-correct round; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0 by round 2; Llama-2 GSM8K 62.0 to 36.5. Gains in prior work used oracle labels.
agent_test: Make every recheck bring new evidence, or a different method; compare against a plain recheck at equal tokens.

claim: Real fault diagnosis by LLM agents is still weak and noise-sensitive: ITBench SRE diagnosis pass@1 13.81% for GPT-4o (9.52% without traces; 36% easy vs 5% hard in the CISO split), AIOpsLab RCA 9-45% across four agents; telemetry dumped raw into context overloads the agent. Cue-conflict effects are not isolated in either.
agent_test: Add seeded cue-conflict variants to a fault-injection suite; test an evidence-summary step.

claim: Order of evidence changes accuracy: premise reorder drops deduction over 30% and GPT-3.5 R-GSM 67.3 to 51.8; document position gives U-shape with worst case below closed-book 56.1%. No test yet in agentic tool loops, and no sorted-summary fix was measured.
agent_test: Shuffle evidence order in a diagnosis loop; test a sorted summary and a permutation vote.

claim: Model scale is not a reliable protection against surface cues: in small open models bigger shortcut more (GPT2-large -33.71% vs base -1.04%), inverse scaling appears in 11 contest tasks incl. one where GPT-4 is below random, but some trends are U-shaped and BiasMedQA found GPT-4 most resilient. No matched scale study on diagnosis cues exists.
agent_test: Run one cue-conflict set across model sizes of one family.

claim: Stated reasoning cannot be trusted to show hint use: when hints change the answer, Claude 3.7 Sonnet verbalises them 25% of the time and DeepSeek R1 39% (20% and 29% for misaligned hints); sycophancy pulls accuracy down by up to 27% when users suggest a wrong answer.
agent_test: Generate hypotheses before reading user hints and compare to hint-first order.

claim: Intuition can be trusted only where the environment is regular and learnable; confidence is not evidence of accuracy. For LLMs the only compute-skipping evidence is in math: later solutions rarely add correct answers (first correct 97% on ASDIV), so easy items can take the fast path. No cue-validity threshold has been measured for fault diagnosis.
agent_test: Measure fast-path accuracy as a function of cue-fault validity in a seeded suite; pick the threshold from data.

claim: Primary Rasmussen/Reason error rates remain unread; no open source found this session gave skill/rule/knowledge-level numbers. Do not cite SRK error rates.
agent_test: Obtain the primary texts before citing any rate.
